values.Plan and process: AggieTrack, the academic planning and advising platform.
Version 1.0, 12 Oct 2026.
James Allred, developer and technical lead. LaDarius Taylor, testing lead. Mellonie Evans, operations. Ivy Mitchell, user experience.
Check sign-in, the curriculum, course planning, prerequisites and paired courses, advisor work, progress, and search. Keep evidence that can be repeated. Mark each result Pass, Fail, or Blocked.

The team is testing the main student and advisor paths: sign-in, academic requirements, course planning, prerequisite checks, degree progress, and advisor work. The plan covers all 10 functional requirements and all 11 non-functional requirements. A feature that is not built yet stays in the plan and is tested when it exists.

This plan does not cover the student information system, financial aid, tuition, or official transcripts. Approving a plan with a PIN, or a student confirming that they registered, is not official enrollment. Production support is out of scope. Draft file uploads, SAR, and WebSocket targets are not acceptance promises.

The Final Requirement Specs are what we accept against. The seed and the code describe how to set the test up, and what the app does today. A gap in the code does not weaken the requirement. The snapshot is commit e96d249, plus local edits in planner/PlanEditor.tsx, planner/page.tsx, and lib/catalog.ts. See source note R-10.

Use an isolated copy of the real stack: Next.js 16.3.4, React 19.2.8, Prisma 7.10.0, and PostgreSQL through the Neon adapter. Better Auth is the version pinned in the lockfile, from the ^1.7.3 range. Resend mail is caught by the test inbox. Redis was not in the runtime that was reviewed. Write down the exact build, schema, and environment. Do not use real student data, and do not run the seed against production.
LaDarius leads testing. James leads the technical work. The tools are a browser, an API client, a read-only database check, a test inbox, a load generator, a way to cause failures, and monitoring.

Safari, Edge, Firefox, and Chrome. Performance runs at 100 Mbps and at 200 Mbps, with the latency written down. The size of the data set has to be approved, and the machine running the load has to be measured. Screen readers, if Q-16 agrees: VoiceOver with Safari, and NVDA with Firefox.

Use the real merged catalog and curriculum from source notes R-02 and R-05. Do not invent courses. Test people use synthetic names and stay private. Fixture D-04 fixes the clock at 2026-10-11 for Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 tests. Use 2026-02-15 when the test needs Spring, Summer, and Fall 2026. Look up course and term ids by code, season, and year. Do not guess an id. Reset only the test student's data, and only in the isolated database.

You need the isolated build, schema, and seed snapshot, verified test accounts, Information Technology and Electronics Technology 2025 profiles, confirmed prior coursework, an advisor assigned in the fixture, the real term rows, and the fixed clock. Review the open decisions on sources, rules, and permissions first. A case may still be run to show a known gap. Mark it Blocked only when the environment or the agreed expected result is missing.

Start with T-01 and T-42 for verification and onboarding. Then T-06, T-07, and T-62 for the catalog. Then T-08 through T-15, plus T-43 through T-49, T-56, T-57, T-58, and T-61, for validation. Then T-19, T-20, T-21, T-51, T-52, and T-59 for progress. Then T-53, T-54, T-55, and T-41 for approval and plan state. Then T-22 through T-29 for access and search, with T-50 and T-60. Then T-16, T-17, and T-18 for the missing advisor workflows. Then T-30 and T-40 for browsers and accessibility. The remaining cases are timing, load, recovery, and encryption.

Every case is Not run after this review of the sources. Pass needs a measured result from the running app or the database, and every agreed check has to hold. Fail means you saw the app break a rule. Blocked means a missing environment, a missing agreed result, or a missing workflow stopped the run. A finding from reading the code is a G item. Do not paste it into Actual result, and do not mark the test Pass or Fail from the code alone. Missing behavior that the requirement asks for does not get acceptance credit.

Every case in scope has been run and passed, with its evidence. There are no open critical or high defects. Any lower defect that remains is accepted in writing by the sponsor. The baseline decisions are resolved, and requirement coverage has been reviewed. A waiver names the scope, the risk, and who approved it. A waiver is not the same as saying the product passed.

When you log a defect, include its id, the build and environment, the test and requirement, the steps, the inputs, what you expected, what happened, the evidence, how severe it is, and who owns the fix. Critical means someone saw data they should not, data was lost, or the app was down. High means a core path is blocked, or degree rules are wrong. Medium means there is a workaround. Low means it is cosmetic. Triage with the test lead and the product owner.

When a fix is ready, write down the new build and link the defect. Reset the same fixture. Repeat the failed case and the nearby boundary tries. Also rerun tests that share the same rule or the same data, plus the smoke set T-01, T-08, T-10, and T-22. Keep the original evidence. Close the defect only after the retest passes and the related checks pass.

Use synthetic data only. Test accounts get the least access they need. Mail stays in the local test inbox. Keep secrets out of this workbook. Remove passwords, tokens, emails, and ids from screenshots and logs. Keep evidence in a restricted store. The proposal is to keep it for 90 days after acceptance, pending Q-15, then delete the fixtures and the evidence under the approved policy.

The source review was read-only. No app tests, database tests, seeds, migrations, or repository edits were run for that review. seed.ts deletes and replaces prerequisite groups and curricula, and it can reassign students. Run it only in a disposable database, after a snapshot. Load and failure tests still need permission, and the stop thresholds from version 1.0 still apply.

Name the evidence with the run id, the test id, and the variant. Include the time in UTC, the tester, the build, the browser and operating system, the seed version, the inputs, screenshots with secrets removed, the API responses, and the relevant database differences and timings. Actual result is what you saw. The evidence reference points at the stored file. Do not invent an outcome.

62 cases cover all 10 functional requirements and all 11 non-functional requirements. The course catalog documents 199 courses the seed can load, plus 3 source rows that are skipped. G-01 through G-14 are findings from reading the code. They are not executed defects. The 500-person test, the daily backup, the encryption evidence, and accessibility on more than one platform still need a staging environment. Fall 2027 is not seeded. Coverage counts come from test status. When a case is added, extend the mapping.

Before this is submitted, the test lead and the academic advisor check every mapping, every expected result, and every fixture. The technical lead checks that the setup can be repeated. The privacy and accessibility owners review the criteria that belong to them. Decisions and owners are recorded under Risks and decisions. At this point every planned test is Not run.

The highlighted cells are filled in while a test is run. On a test, enter the actual result, the status, the defect id, the evidence reference, who ran it, and the date. Write the exact build and environment in the evidence. On a defect, keep the finding and what the retest showed.

values.Test / scenario: Sign up, choose Information Technology 2025, and keep CST 130 on the plan
values.Preconditions: A new email for student A; A test inbox that only this run can see; Fixtures D-01, D-02, and D-04
values.Inputs / data: A test first and last name; student.a@example.test; A test password of at least 8 characters; Information Technology, program INFO 0432, catalog 2025; CST 130, 3 credits
values.Procedure:
1. Register from the public page and confirm the verification email.
2. Open /enter, continue to onboarding, and choose Information Technology 2025.
3. On /student/progress, confirm there is no prior coursework.
4. Acknowledge the current-semester prompt and add CST 130 to Spring 2027.
5. Sign out, sign back in, and reload the planner.
values.Expected result: The account is verified and has the student role; There is one Information Technology 2025 profile; The selected plan has one CST 130 row
values.Pass criterion: Verification and onboarding both finish; After signing in again, CST 130 is still there once, at 3 credits; Student B's data is not on this account
values.Evidence to retain: Screenshots with personal details removed; The account id; The plan before and after

values.Test / scenario: Turn away a bad login
values.Preconditions: Student A is already verified; The public sign-in dialog is available; Each try starts from a signed-out browser
values.Inputs / data: The right email with the wrong password, at least 8 characters; An email that has no account; A blank email; A blank password; An email that is not a valid address; A password of 7 characters
values.Procedure:
1. Submit each pair on its own.
2. After each rejection, try a plan URL and a protected action directly.
values.Expected result: Each bad try is rejected; No session is created; Academic data stays hidden
values.Pass criterion: All six tries are rejected by the form or the server; The protected student page shows no academic data; The protected action returns no academic data
values.Evidence to retain: The responses, with secrets removed; The session state after each try

values.Test / scenario: Reset a password and keep the plan
values.Preconditions: Student A is verified and already has CST 130 saved; The test inbox catches the reset email
values.Inputs / data: Student A's email on /reset; The link from that email, opened at /reset/password; A new matching password of at least 8 characters
values.Procedure:
1. Request a reset at /reset.
2. Open the link from the test inbox and enter the new password twice.
3. Sign out.
4. Try the old password, then the new one.
5. Reload the Spring 2027 plan.
values.Expected result: The reset finishes; The old password is rejected and the new one works; The saved plan is unchanged
values.Pass criterion: Exactly one reset email arrives; The old password is rejected; The new password is accepted; The saved plan is the same
values.Evidence to retain: The email details, with the token removed; The sign-in results, with secrets removed

values.Test / scenario: Reject a reset link that is expired, reused, or invalid
values.Preconditions: Confirm how long the pinned Better Auth reset link actually lasts; The screen says the link lasts one hour; Use a separate link for each try, and control the clock
values.Inputs / data: A reset link checked at 59 minutes 59 seconds; A reset link checked at 60 minutes 1 second; A token that was already used; A token that was never issued; A password of 7 characters; A confirmation that does not match
values.Procedure:
1. Check two different tokens at the times above.
2. Use a valid token once, then try it again.
3. Submit a bad token, a short password, and a mismatched confirmation.
4. Confirm the password did not change after the rejected tries.
values.Expected result: A link still inside the hour works; An expired, reused, or invalid link is rejected; A short or mismatched password is rejected
values.Pass criterion: The one-hour promise on the screen matches the real expiry; None of the bad tries change the password; After a successful reset, the old password no longer works
values.Evidence to retain: The error responses, with tokens removed; The time and the expiry that was configured; The sign-in checks

values.Test / scenario: Stop a second account from colliding with the first
values.Preconditions: Student A already has an account and a saved plan
values.Inputs / data: Student A's existing email; The same email with different letter case, if the team has agreed that case should not matter
values.Procedure:
1. Try to register again with each version of the email.
2. Sign in to the original account.
3. Compare the number of accounts and the saved plan.
values.Expected result: A verified account is not created a second time; An unverified account gets another verification email, if that is how the hook is set
values.Pass criterion: There is still one account, and the plan is not merged with another; The original data is unchanged; Write down the verified try and the unverified try separately
values.Evidence to retain: The account count; The plan comparison

values.Test / scenario: Show the Information Technology 2025 handbook and course groups
values.Preconditions: Fixture D-02 is loaded in its own database; The profile is INFO 0432 and the start term is confirmed
values.Inputs / data: Information Technology 2025; The handbook on /student/planner; The course list on /student/courses
values.Procedure:
1. Compare all 13 requirement groups with info-2025.ts.
2. Check the 22 named core courses, their credits, and the 8 recommended semesters.
3. Check the general education, management, technical, and free-elective placeholders.
4. Compare the summary total with program.totalCredits.
values.Expected result: Information Technology requires 120 credits; The groups are major 56, mathematics 11, writing 6, college success 1, speech 3, business 3, management 6, global awareness 3, African American studies 3, social and behavioral sciences 3, scientific reasoning 7, technical 12, and free 6; Each of the four technical slots is 3 credits
values.Pass criterion: The 13 group minimums add up to 120; All 22 core rows match the seed; All 8 semesters and the right slot credits are shown; Write down the PDF total of 117 credits as gap G-11
values.Evidence to retain: An export of the curriculum; A row-by-row comparison

values.Test / scenario: Keep Information Technology and Electronics Technology requirements apart
values.Preconditions: Student A is onboarded to INFO 0432, catalog 2025; Student B is onboarded to ELET 0340, catalog 2025; There is no screen for switching programs, so use two accounts
values.Inputs / data: Information Technology major core is 56 credits, and technical electives are 12; Electronics Technology major core is 54 credits, technical electives are 9 and must be CST 200 or above; Electronics Technology mathematics is 15 credits and physics is 8
values.Procedure:
1. Sign in as student A and write down the handbook groups.
2. Sign in separately as student B and write down those groups.
3. Compare each set with its own curriculum source.
4. Reload both accounts and compare the profiles.
values.Expected result: Each student sees their own program and the 2025 catalog; The core and elective rules stay different; Both programs total 120 credits
values.Pass criterion: Both sets match the right seed; Neither student sees the other student's profile; Electronics Technology includes MATH 132 and PHYS 225, 235, 226, and 236, and Information Technology does not
values.Evidence to retain: The program ids; The dashboards and records before and after

values.Test / scenario: Add a valid course and find it still there after a reload
values.Preconditions: Student A is a verified Information Technology student; CST 130 is not on the transcript or the plan; The clock is 2026-10-11 at 12:00 UTC, Fall 2026 is acknowledged, and Spring 2027 is open
values.Inputs / data: CST 130, Introduction to Unix/Linux, 3 credits, Spring 2027
values.Procedure:
1. Search for CST 130 in the planner.
2. Add it to the Spring 2027 draft.
3. Reload and read the saved planned course on its own.
values.Expected result: CST 130 is added once to the draft; It is saved at 3 credits; It is still there after a reload
values.Pass criterion: One planned course points at the real CST 130 id and the Spring 2027 term id; There is no error
values.Evidence to retain: The screen after the add; The saved record; The request id

values.Test / scenario: Reject a course that is a duplicate or not a real choice
values.Preconditions: Fixtures D-02 and D-04; CST 130 is already on the Spring 2027 draft; The clock is 2026-10-11 at 12:00 UTC, Fall 2026 is acknowledged, and Spring 2027 is open
values.Inputs / data: The same CST 130 again; A course id that does not exist; CST 130 already on the Fall 2026 plan; CST 130 already completed on the transcript; CST 130 already in progress on the transcript
values.Procedure:
1. Reset the fixture before each try.
2. Submit the add through the signed-in action.
3. Compare the plan count, the transcript count, and the error on the screen.
values.Expected result: A duplicate in the same term is rejected; A missing course is rejected; A course already planned in another term is rejected; A completed or in-progress transcript course is rejected
values.Pass criterion: All five tries fail and do not add a row; The error says whether the problem is this term, another term, the transcript, or a bad course
values.Evidence to retain: The action responses; The message on the screen; The plan before and after

values.Test / scenario: Remove a planned course
values.Preconditions: Student A's Spring 2027 draft includes CST 130; The transcript is unchanged; A submitted-plan version of this is covered by T-55
values.Inputs / data: The planned-course id for CST 130, not the catalog course id
values.Procedure:
1. Write down the draft and the transcript.
2. Remove CST 130 with the remove control.
3. Reload, sign in again, and compare the records.
values.Expected result: Only that draft row for CST 130 is removed; The catalog is unchanged; The academic history is unchanged
values.Pass criterion: That CST 130 row is gone from the plan; The transcript and catalog are unchanged; Student B's plan is untouched
values.Evidence to retain: The plan before and after; The academic record before and after

values.Test / scenario: Remove a prerequisite that a later course still needs
values.Preconditions: Fixture D-04 sets the clock; Student A has CST 120 on the Fall 2026 draft; CST 112 and CST 122 are on the Spring 2027 draft; MATH 110 is not on the transcript or the plan
values.Inputs / data: Remove CST 120 from Fall 2026, then try to submit Spring 2027
values.Procedure:
1. Confirm CST 112 was allowed because CST 120 was planned earlier.
2. Remove CST 120 from Fall.
3. Reload the Spring plan.
4. Try to submit it and have an advisor review it.
values.Expected result: The later course should be blocked or clearly flagged before anyone approves it; Removing the earlier course and submitting the later one does not recheck the dependency today
values.Pass criterion: The behavior matches the signed decision in Q-04; CST 112 is never quietly approved when neither CST 120 nor MATH 110 is satisfied
values.Evidence to retain: The validation message; The plan before and after

values.Test / scenario: Reject CST 112 when the prerequisite is missing
values.Preconditions: Student A does not have MATH 110 or CST 120 on a qualifying transcript or an earlier plan; The clock is 2026-10-11 at 12:00 UTC, Fall 2026 is acknowledged, and Spring 2027 is open
values.Inputs / data: CST 112 with its lab CST 122, planned for Spring 2027
values.Procedure:
1. Search in the course browser and in the planner.
2. Try to add both real course ids through the server action.
3. Look at the saved plan.
values.Expected result: CST 112 is rejected because neither prerequisite is met; Neither the lecture nor the lab is saved
values.Pass criterion: The action reports a prerequisite error; The save writes zero rows for CST 112 and CST 122; The eligibility search leaves the course out, as FR-10 requires
values.Evidence to retain: The error on the screen and from the action; The database query

values.Test / scenario: Check when a prerequisite counts, including the transcript
values.Preconditions: Each try uses its own fixture; MATH 110 is not available as the other option; The clock is 2026-10-11 at 12:00 UTC, Fall 2026 is acknowledged, and Spring 2027 is open
values.Inputs / data: CST 112 and CST 122 aimed at Spring 2027; CST 120 completed in an earlier term; CST 120 only on an earlier draft; CST 120 on the same Spring 2027 plan; CST 120 on a later Summer 2027 plan; CST 120 failed on the transcript; CST 120 in progress on the transcript
values.Procedure:
1. Set up one CST 120 situation.
2. Try to add CST 112 with CST 122.
3. Write down the result and reset.
4. Compare all six results with the signed policy and with what the code does today.
values.Expected result: The code accepts a completed or in-progress transcript, and any earlier planned course; It rejects a failed course, and a prerequisite planned in the same term or a later term; The academic owner still has to approve whether an in-progress course should count
values.Pass criterion: The six results match the signed decision in Q-04; A rejected try saves neither course; If the code and the policy disagree, write that down as a defect
values.Evidence to retain: A six-row table of the results; A snapshot of each plan

values.Test / scenario: Require CST 112 and CST 122 in the same term
values.Preconditions: MATH 110 is completed; CST 112 and CST 122 are not on the transcript; The clock is 2026-10-11 at 12:00 UTC, Fall 2026 is acknowledged, and Spring 2027 is open
values.Inputs / data: CST 122 by itself; CST 112 and CST 122 together; CST 112 already on an earlier plan; CST 112 on a later plan; CST 112 already completed
values.Procedure:
1. Reset before each try.
2. Try to add CST 122 to Spring 2027 from the course browser and from the action.
3. Check the exact course and term ids that were saved.
values.Expected result: The pair in the same term is allowed; A missing companion, or a companion in another term, is rejected unless a completed companion was approved as an exception; The screen currently lets you add the lab alone, and the server does not enforce the pair
values.Pass criterion: Each try matches Q-04; A lecture or lab does not stay on the plan by itself unless that exception was approved; A valid pair is 3 credits plus 1 credit, 4 in total
values.Evidence to retain: The result of each try; The messages on the screen; The terms that were saved

values.Test / scenario: Removing one course of a pair should not hide the problem
values.Preconditions: MATH 110 is completed; CST 112 and CST 122 are both on the Spring 2027 draft; Neither course is already completed
values.Inputs / data: Remove CST 112 and leave CST 122; Then the other way: remove CST 122 and leave CST 112
values.Procedure:
1. Remove one of the pair.
2. Reload.
3. Try to submit the term, then try an advisor approval.
4. Reset and repeat with the other course removed.
values.Expected result: The plan should be blocked or clearly flagged before approval; Today, each course can be removed on its own, and submission does not check the pair again
values.Pass criterion: Both tries follow the signed rule in Q-04; An invalid pair is not approved without a flag
values.Evidence to retain: The plan; The message on the screen

values.Test / scenario: An advisor changes an assigned student's plan by hand
values.Preconditions: Advisor A-1 is assigned to student A; Student A is in Information Technology and has a Spring 2027 plan; CST 130 is not on that plan; Gap G-05 is the known missing workflow
values.Inputs / data: The advisor adds CST 130 for student A, then removes it
values.Procedure:
1. Open /advisor/plans and find student A's plan.
2. Look for a way to edit the courses by hand.
3. Add CST 130 and confirm it as student A.
4. Remove it and confirm that too.
5. If that workflow is not there, write down the FR-06 gap and do not treat approval as a substitute.
values.Expected result: A manual change should stick for the assigned student; The code that was reviewed can approve a plan and enter a PIN; A way for the advisor to add or remove a course was not found
values.Pass criterion: The advisor can add and remove the course, and the student can see the change; Student B is unchanged; If the workflow is missing, FR-06 is not accepted
values.Evidence to retain: The advisor screen and the student screen; The plan before and after

values.Test / scenario: Save an advisor comment and have it still be there
values.Preconditions: Advisor A-1 is assigned to student A; The AdvisingNote model exists; No save action for comments was found in the app that was reviewed
values.Inputs / data: Comment: Complete MATH 110 or CST 120 before CST 112.; Feedback: Take CST 122 with CST 112.
values.Procedure:
1. Find the comment editor for student A.
2. Save both notes.
3. Reload the advisor view and the student view.
4. Check who wrote them and who can see them.
5. If there is no editor, write down the missing FR-06 behavior.
values.Expected result: Both notes stay saved and are attributed to advisor A-1; A note the student is allowed to see reaches student A only; Placeholder notes on the dashboard are not proof that a comment was saved
values.Pass criterion: The saved note matches the text and the visibility after a reload; Student B cannot see it; If the editor is missing, this does not pass
values.Evidence to retain: Both screens, with personal details removed; The saved comment records

values.Test / scenario: Advisor edits have to follow the same course rules
values.Preconditions: Advisor A-1 is assigned to student A; Student A has neither MATH 110 nor CST 120; A manual edit workflow was not found in the reviewed app
values.Inputs / data: The advisor tries to add CST 112 and CST 122
values.Procedure:
1. Use the advisor edit path if it exists.
2. If you are testing the action directly, submit the invalid courses while signed in as the advisor.
3. Check the saved plan and the error.
4. Write down a missing path separately from a permission denial.
values.Expected result: A future manual edit has to use the same prerequisite rule, or record an approved override with the advisor's name; Approving a plan is not the same as editing its courses
values.Pass criterion: An invalid edit is never saved quietly; A missing manual edit stays gap G-05; This test does not pass just because approval works
values.Evidence to retain: The error, or the approved override; The plan query

values.Test / scenario: Show Information Technology progress at 0, 3, 6, and 120 credits
values.Preconditions: Fixture D-05 is an independent check of the 120-credit Information Technology audit; Core courses need at least a C; Q-05 has agreed how credits are counted and rounded; The dashboard stuck at zero is gap G-04
values.Inputs / data: No completed courses; CST 120 completed, 3 credits; CST 120 and CST 130 completed, 6 credits; A full 120-credit Information Technology fixture, with each course counted once
values.Procedure:
1. Load each transcript fixture on its own.
2. Open the student dashboard.
3. Compare the completed credits and the percent with the independent check.
4. Save a screenshot and reset.
values.Expected result: 0 of 120 is 0%; 3 of 120 is 2.5%; 6 of 120 is 5%; 120 of 120 is 100%; The dashboard currently uses a hard-coded zero
values.Pass criterion: All four states show the agreed credit total and percent; A dashboard that stays at zero while courses are complete is a fail
values.Evidence to retain: The fixture and the independent calculation; Screenshots of the dashboard

values.Test / scenario: Leave out failed, repeated, and unused credit
values.Preconditions: Fixture D-05, Information Technology; The counting rules in Q-05 are approved; Failed grades are loaded only in this isolated fixture, because there is no failed-grade screen
values.Inputs / data: CST 120 completed with a C; CST 120 entered a second time; CST 130 failed with an F; CST 140 in progress; CST 101 not placed in any elective slot
values.Procedure:
1. Add each extra record in its own fixture.
2. Recompute the completed credits that should count.
3. Refresh the dashboard and compare.
4. Test elective credit on its own, after it has been assigned to a slot.
values.Expected result: The base stays 3 of 120, which is 2.5%; Each course is counted once; CST 101 counts only after it is placed in an elective that allows it
values.Pass criterion: Nothing is counted twice; Failed, in-progress, and unassigned credit is left out; An approved elective adds only the credits that slot allows; A dashboard stuck at zero stays gap G-04
values.Evidence to retain: Each transcript variant; The independent calculation

values.Test / scenario: Progress changes when a completion changes
values.Preconditions: The Information Technology student has CST 120 marked complete on /student/progress; CST 130 is still blank; Q-05 is approved
values.Inputs / data: Mark CST 130 complete, then clear it; Leave CST 120 complete
values.Procedure:
1. Confirm the applicable completed credits start at 3.
2. Mark CST 130 complete and save.
3. Refresh /student and check the transcript.
4. Clear CST 130, save, and refresh again.
values.Expected result: The transcript adds CST 130 and then removes it; The degree percent should move from 2.5% to 5% and back to 2.5%; The dashboard is currently stuck at zero
values.Pass criterion: Both changes stick; The percent on the screen matches the agreed total after each refresh
values.Evidence to retain: The dashboard at each step, with the time; The record before and after

values.Test / scenario: Signed-out visitors cannot open protected pages or actions
values.Preconditions: The browser is signed out; The pages to try are /student, /student/progress, /student/courses, /student/planner, /advisor/plans, and /admin; The server actions to try are the real add, remove, save-progress, and approve actions
values.Inputs / data: Page requests with no session; Action requests with no session
values.Procedure:
1. Visit each protected page while signed out.
2. Call each action with a saved request and no session.
3. Compare the data afterward.
values.Expected result: Each page asks for a sign-in; Reads and writes without a session are rejected; No academic data is returned
values.Pass criterion: Every route and action refuses the data; No planned course, transcript row, or plan status changes; The public sign-in pages still work
values.Evidence to retain: The list of routes and what each returned; The responses, with secrets removed; The database before and after

values.Test / scenario: Signing out ends the session
values.Preconditions: Student A is signed in; A protected response was captured earlier, with the token removed
values.Inputs / data: Use Sign out; Then replay the old session from a separate test client
values.Procedure:
1. Sign out.
2. Open a protected page again.
3. Replay the saved session against a plan read and a plan write.
values.Expected result: The old session cannot read protected data; The old session cannot change protected data
values.Pass criterion: The screen asks for a sign-in; The replay is rejected; Saved data is unchanged
values.Evidence to retain: The response codes; The session results, with secrets removed

values.Test / scenario: Validation messages tell the person what to fix
values.Preconditions: For the prerequisite try, MATH 110 and CST 120 are both missing; For the other try, CST 122 has no companion; The clock is 2026-10-11 at 12:00 UTC, Fall 2026 is acknowledged, and Spring 2027 is open
values.Inputs / data: CST 112 blocked by prerequisites; CST 122 alone; Then fix it by completing CST 120 and adding CST 112 with CST 122
values.Procedure:
1. Trigger each invalid choice from the action and from the screen, if the screen can do it.
2. Write down the inline error or toast.
3. Fix the prerequisite and the pair, then try again.
values.Expected result: The prerequisite error and the missing-pair error can be told apart; The valid pair saves; The missing-pair error is the known gap G-02
values.Pass criterion: Both invalid saves are refused, and the message says what to do; The corrected pair saves once; A general prerequisite message is enough if it says the cause and what to do next, even if it does not name the course
values.Evidence to retain: The error and the success message; The saved records

values.Test / scenario: A failed save shows an error and does not pretend it worked
values.Preconditions: Use an isolated stand-in that can fail a write, and take a snapshot first; CST 130 is a normal valid add and remove; Do not use the production database; The clock is 2026-10-11 at 12:00 UTC, Fall 2026 is acknowledged, and Spring 2027 is open
values.Inputs / data: Add CST 130 to Spring 2027, and have the database reject the write; Remove a course, and delay the response past 15 seconds
values.Procedure:
1. Try a valid add while the save is set to fail.
2. Repeat a removal and delay the response past 15 seconds.
3. Restore the service, refresh, and compare the screen with what was saved.
values.Expected result: If the save cannot finish within 15 seconds, the person sees an error; The screen then matches what was actually saved
values.Pass criterion: There is no false success; Each case shows a clear error; The saved state matches the screen after refresh; Trying again does not create a duplicate
values.Evidence to retain: The timing; The error message; The database compared with the screen

values.Test / scenario: Planner search only suggests courses the student can take
values.Preconditions: An Information Technology student is missing MATH 110 and CST 120; The transcript is empty and Spring 2027 is a draft; The clock is 2026-10-11 at 12:00 UTC, Fall 2026 is acknowledged, and Spring 2027 is open
values.Inputs / data: Search the planner for CST 130, CST 112, CST 212, and CST 225; Repeat as the advisor if a search in the student's context exists
values.Procedure:
1. Open search on /student/planner and enter each exact code. Each code is at least 2 characters.
2. Compare the suggestions with the set you expected.
3. Try the same search as the assigned advisor.
4. If the advisor search is not there, write that down.
values.Expected result: CST 130 is eligible; CST 112 is left out because neither alternative is met; CST 212 is left out because of its prerequisite and the term it is offered; CST 225 is eligible because CST 235 can be added with it; An advisor search in the student's context, which FR-10 asks for, was not found
values.Pass criterion: The student's four results match those decisions; The advisor can search the same context, or the gap stays written down under FR-10
values.Evidence to retain: The search text; The student and term ids; The suggestions compared with the expected set

values.Test / scenario: Search results change when the term or the student's progress changes
values.Preconditions: The clock is 2026-02-15, during Spring 2026; Acknowledge the current semester; Summer 2026 and Fall 2026 are available as targets; The profile is Information Technology
values.Inputs / data: CST 306 requires CST 140; CST 325 requires CST 225; CST 496 is offered in Fall only; Change a completion or an earlier planned course between searches
values.Procedure:
1. Search the exact codes in the planner for a Spring target, then for Summer and Fall.
2. Write down what is eligible while the prerequisites are missing.
3. Mark CST 140 and CST 225 complete and refresh.
4. Search again and compare the term with the requirements.
5. Clear the completion and refresh again.
values.Expected result: CST 306 and CST 325 become eligible in Summer or Fall only after the prerequisite is met; CST 496 is offered in Fall only, and only with the approved standing; Do not look for a department filter. That control is not in the app
values.Pass criterion: After every refresh, the results match the approved prerequisite and term rules; A suggestion does not linger after its prerequisite is removed
values.Evidence to retain: The searches and their results; The fixture used for each try

values.Test / scenario: Search matches, empty queries, and the planner's limit
values.Preconditions: An Information Technology student with fixture D-02 loaded; The course browser is /student/courses; The planner search is limited to courses the student can take this term; Prerequisites are set for the tries that need them
values.Inputs / data: cst 130 and CST 130; Unix; Technical Electives; zzz-no-course; An empty query; A single character; A broad CST query in the planner
values.Procedure:
1. In the browser, search by exact code, by title, and by group name. Wait for the 250 millisecond pause and for the list to finish rendering.
2. Try a query with no match, then clear the query.
3. In the planner, search with one character, then with a broad CST query.
4. Write down each result set.
values.Expected result: The browser matches code, title, or description without caring about letter case, and it can match a whole group name; An empty query shows the sections; A query with no match shows the empty state; The planner needs at least 2 characters and shows at most 8 suggestions
values.Pass criterion: cst 130 and CST 130 find the same course; A title search finds the right course; A group name shows that group's courses; A query with no match shows nothing; One character in the planner shows nothing, and a broad query shows 8 or fewer
values.Evidence to retain: The query; What came back

values.Test / scenario: A student or advisor cannot open someone else's plan
values.Preconditions: Student A and student B each have a profile; Advisor A-1 is assigned only to student A; Advisor A-2 is assigned only to student B; Use the real page layouts and the ownership checks on the actions
values.Inputs / data: Student A tries to remove a planned course that belongs to student B; Student A tries to submit student B's plan; Advisor A-1 tries to approve student B's submitted plan; Student A tries to call the advisor approve action
values.Procedure:
1. Try each case from the page and from the signed-in action.
2. Open the other role's section directly.
3. Check both students' data before and after.
values.Expected result: Every unauthorized try is denied; No plan or comment from the other person is shown
values.Pass criterion: All four tries fail on the server; The wrong role is sent back to its home page; No plan, PIN, or academic record is returned or changed
values.Evidence to retain: A table of who tried what; The responses, with secrets removed; The database before and after

values.Test / scenario: The main workflow works in each supported browser
values.Preconditions: Use the same build and the same fixtures in every browser; Use the latest stable Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari that Q-11 approves, and write down the operating system
values.Inputs / data: Sign-in and onboarding are already done; View the Information Technology requirements; Search, add, and remove CST 130; Submit the plan; The assigned advisor approves it and enters a PIN; Sign out
values.Procedure:
1. Reset the fixture for each browser and operating system.
2. Run the workflow that is actually built.
3. Compare the plan status, the rows, the PIN, and the controls.
values.Expected result: The same actions lead to the same outcome in each supported browser; The controls can be used in each of those browsers
values.Pass criterion: Every built action passes in each supported browser; The missing advisor comment and edit workflow stays gap G-05; Do not leave that gap out of the notes just because the rest passed
values.Evidence to retain: The browser and operating system versions; A table of the workflow in each browser; Screenshots

values.Test / scenario: Pages still load within 5 seconds with 500 people active
values.Preconditions: An isolated deployment of the real Next.js 16.3.4 app; PostgreSQL through the adapter in lib/prisma.ts; The 199-course snapshot and the 2025 Information Technology and Electronics Technology curricula; Q-12 has approved the capacity target
values.Inputs / data: 500 active sessions; About 70% students and 30% advisors; First 100 Mbps, then 200 Mbps; Fixture D-07
values.Procedure:
1. Run a baseline with 1 user.
2. Ramp through 50, 100, 250, and 500.
3. Hold 500 users for 10 minutes at each speed.
4. Measure from the start of navigation until the main content is usable, for the dashboard, the program, the plan, and search.
values.Expected result: Pages load within 5 seconds at those speeds and with that many people
values.Pass criterion: Every sampled page load is 5 seconds or less; No request fails and no acknowledged write is lost; Report the percentiles and the slowest load; Q-12 decides what counts as the app not slowing down
values.Evidence to retain: The load script; The size of the data set; The traces; The slowest load, the 95th percentile, and the error log

values.Test / scenario: An add or a remove is saved within 15 seconds
values.Preconditions: Fixture D-04, on an isolated load setup that has been approved; A separate read checks what was actually saved; CST 130 is absent for the add, and present for the remove; The clock is 2026-10-11 at 12:00 UTC, Fall 2026 is acknowledged, and Spring 2027 is open
values.Inputs / data: 30 separate add-and-remove pairs for CST 130 in Spring 2027; Repeat at 500 active users if the environment can do it
values.Procedure:
1. Time the gap from submit until a separate read sees the committed add or removal.
2. Repeat 30 pairs, starting from a clean draft each time.
3. Check the planned-course count and that the plan is still a draft.
4. Write down the normal run and the 500-user run separately.
values.Expected result: Every successful change is saved within 15 seconds
values.Pass criterion: All 60 operations at normal load finish within 15 seconds; The final state matches what was requested; The 500-user results are written down on their own; Errors are shown clearly
values.Evidence to retain: The time of the submit, the commit, and the read-back; The request ids; The final difference

values.Test / scenario: Sign out after 30 minutes with no activity
values.Preconditions: Student A is signed in; The team has agreed what counts as activity; Write down the time of the last real action
values.Inputs / data: A protected request at 29 minutes 59 seconds; A protected request at 30 minutes 1 second; Use a separate session for each
values.Procedure:
1. Leave two sessions idle, and do not let a background check reset the timer.
2. Check one at 29 minutes 59 seconds and the other at 30 minutes 1 second.
3. After the later one expires, try a read and a write.
values.Expected result: The session still inside 30 minutes works; The session past 30 minutes does not
values.Pass criterion: The first session is still valid; The second session is asked to sign in; An expired session does not change any data
values.Evidence to retain: The clock and the timestamps; The responses, with secrets removed

values.Test / scenario: Real activity starts the 30 minutes over
values.Preconditions: Q-08 has agreed what counts as activity; Student A has a session
values.Inputs / data: A real user action at 20 minutes; Then more idle time
values.Procedure:
1. Do a qualifying action at minute 20.
2. Check access at minute 35.
3. In a separate run, do nothing else and check at 50 minutes 1 second.
values.Expected result: A real action resets the timer; The session ends 30 minutes after the last real action
values.Pass criterion: Access at minute 35 works; In the separate run, access at 50 minutes 1 second is denied
values.Evidence to retain: When the activity happened; When the session expired

values.Test / scenario: Common tasks take fewer than five clicks
values.Preconditions: The proposed group is 5 students and 3 advisors; People have agreed to take part; They are already signed in; The starting screen and the reset are written down before you begin
values.Inputs / data: From the dashboard, open the Information Technology handbook; From the planner, add CST 130; Remove CST 130; Search the catalog for the exact code CST 130; From /advisor/plans, an advisor approves a submitted plan
values.Procedure:
1. Give each person one real task and do not coach them.
2. Start at the screen you specified.
3. Count every click or tap, including opening a dialog, choosing an item, and submitting.
4. Write down success and the click count for every try. Do not add a department-filter task. That control is not in the app.
values.Expected result: Each person finishes the task in fewer than 5 clicks, using the counting rule that was approved
values.Pass criterion: A finished task uses at most 4 clicks; A task the person cannot finish is a fail, not a blank; Keep the person and the task with the result
values.Evidence to retain: The click log, with names removed; The consent record; What people said afterward

values.Test / scenario: A daily backup can be restored
values.Preconditions: An isolated PostgreSQL database, on Neon or another PostgreSQL host; Fixtures D-01, D-02, and D-04; The backup schedule and what it includes have been supplied; No daily backup job was found in the application files that were reviewed
values.Inputs / data: Two daily backups in a row; A separate restored copy
values.Procedure:
1. Check the time and the status of two daily backup cycles.
2. Restore the latest backup into an empty isolated database.
3. Compare the counts and a hash of the important records.
values.Expected result: Each day's backup finishes; Plans, academic records, curriculum, and comments come back intact
values.Pass criterion: There is one successful backup each day; The restored ids, counts, and hashes match the backup; The restored app can open the plans
values.Evidence to retain: The job logs; The list of what was backed up; The restore log and the comparison

values.Test / scenario: The app is usable again within three minutes, without losing saved work
values.Preconditions: The failure targets for the app and the database are approved and isolated; A snapshot of fixtures D-01 and D-04; Known CST 130 adds and removals that have already been saved; A health check and a check that a person can still do the work
values.Inputs / data: Stop the app, then separately break the database connection; Have one save in flight for each case
values.Procedure:
1. Write down what is already saved.
2. Cause the failure and start the timer.
3. Bring the service back.
4. Check sign-in, reading, and writing, and compare the data.
5. Sort out the save that was in flight.
values.Expected result: The service is usable again within 180 seconds; Academic data that was already saved is still there
values.Pass criterion: Each recovery finishes within 180 seconds; Saved records are unchanged; The in-flight save has a clear outcome, and retrying it does not create a duplicate
values.Evidence to retain: When the failure started and when the service returned; The health check and the functional check; Hashes of the records

values.Test / scenario: 500 people at once do not mix up each other's plans
values.Preconditions: Fixture D-07, with a unique user and plan for each session; The 500-session target is approved; A baseline data set is loaded
values.Inputs / data: 500 people at the same time, reading and making valid adds and removals
values.Procedure:
1. Ramp up to 500 active sessions.
2. Run the agreed mix of work for 10 minutes.
3. Match every person's actions to what was saved.
4. Compare speed and errors with the baseline.
values.Expected result: Nobody sees another person's data; A change that was acknowledged is not lost; A write is not saved twice; The approved speed limits still hold
values.Pass criterion: Every final plan matches that person's list of actions; Nothing leaks and no request fails; Pages stay within 5 seconds and saves stay within 15 seconds; Agree how much slowdown is acceptable before you call the result
values.Evidence to retain: Each person's list of actions; The final difference; Resource use and response times

values.Test / scenario: Plans are encrypted on the way and where they are stored
values.Preconditions: You can see the transport and storage settings on staging; Use a made-up degree plan; A privacy reviewer is assigned
values.Inputs / data: HTTPS for the plan and schedule actions; The PostgreSQL or Neon store, and the provider's backups; Sessions, PINs, and logs; Redis was not in the app that was reviewed
values.Procedure:
1. List the stores that actually hold academic data.
2. Check HTTPS and the TLS settings that were approved.
3. Check encryption on the database and on provider backups, and who can use the keys.
4. Try to open a plan or a PIN without permission, and check that logs are cleaned.
5. Write down any hosting evidence you cannot get from the code.
values.Expected result: Every plan and schedule path in scope meets the approved encryption and access rules
values.Pass criterion: Nothing in scope travels as plain text; Every store and backup in scope has evidence of encryption; Someone without permission cannot read the keys or the data; The privacy review is signed
values.Evidence to retain: Transport and config evidence, with secrets removed; The list of stores; The privacy review

values.Test / scenario: The same work can be done with a keyboard and a screen reader
values.Preconditions: The WCAG version and level are approved; VoiceOver with Safari, and NVDA with Firefox, are available; Fixture D-04
values.Inputs / data: Public email verification and sign-in; The Information Technology handbook; Search, add, and remove CST 130; The prerequisite error for CST 112; Choosing the CST 112 and CST 122 pair; An advisor entering a PIN to approve
values.Procedure:
1. Do every built workflow with the keyboard only.
2. Repeat with VoiceOver on Safari and with NVDA on Firefox.
3. Check focus in the search popover, dialogs, and whether errors and toasts are announced.
4. Walk the approved checklist. Test advisor comments separately, when that screen exists.
values.Expected result: Every listed task can be finished; Controls and errors are announced; Focus is visible, follows a sensible order, and never gets trapped
values.Pass criterion: All tasks finish on both screen-reader pairs; There are no open failures against the approved criteria
values.Evidence to retain: The task and criteria table; The screen-reader versions; Recordings with personal details removed

values.Test / scenario: A student cannot save over a plan the advisor has already taken
values.Preconditions: Spring 2027 is a draft that includes CST 130; Student A has the plan open in two tabs; Advisor A-1 is assigned; The saved plan id is known
values.Inputs / data: A stale add or remove from the student; The plan moves from draft to submitted, then to approved; The test PIN is TEST1234
values.Procedure:
1. Open the same draft in two student tabs.
2. Submit it from the first tab.
3. From the stale second tab, try to add or remove a course, and confirm it is rejected.
4. Approve the plan as advisor A-1.
5. Replay the stale request, and also try a submit and a write at the same time, through the action.
values.Expected result: The lock is enforced when the change is saved; A stale write does not change the course list of a submitted or approved plan; Today the status is checked before the write transaction, so this still needs a concurrency check
values.Pass criterion: Nothing is saved after the plan is locked; The courses the advisor wrote to the transcript match the approved plan; Both student tabs agree after a reload
values.Evidence to retain: The version and request ids; The conflict message; The final plan

values.Test / scenario: A student has to verify email and finish onboarding
values.Preconditions: Student A is new and not verified yet; Fixtures D-01 and D-02; Mail is caught only by the test inbox
values.Inputs / data: A sign-in attempt before verification; A verified user with no profile; A profile whose prior coursework is not confirmed
values.Procedure:
1. Try to sign in before the email is verified.
2. Verify the email and open /enter.
3. Choose Information Technology 2025.
4. Try /student/courses before confirming progress.
5. Confirm there is no prior coursework.
values.Expected result: An unverified sign-in is refused; No profile sends the person to onboarding; An unconfirmed start sends the person to /student/progress; A confirmed student can open courses
values.Pass criterion: Each state sends the person to the right place; There is only one profile; startConfirmedAt is set once
values.Evidence to retain: The screen; The action response, with secrets removed; The database before and after

values.Test / scenario: CST 112 accepts either prerequisite
values.Preconditions: The clock is 2026-10-11 at 12:00 UTC, Fall 2026 is acknowledged, and Spring 2027 is open; Reset between tries; The prerequisite you are not testing is absent
values.Inputs / data: CST 112 and CST 122 in Spring 2027; Only MATH 110 completed; Only CST 120 completed; Neither completed; Both completed
values.Procedure:
1. Set up each of the four situations.
2. Add CST 112 and CST 122 together.
3. Check the rows and the credits, then reset.
values.Expected result: MATH 110 or CST 120 is enough; If neither is done, the add is rejected
values.Pass criterion: MATH 110 alone is allowed, CST 120 alone is allowed, neither is rejected, and both is allowed; A valid pair is exactly 4 credits; A rejected try saves zero rows
values.Evidence to retain: The screen; The action response, with secrets removed; The database before and after

values.Test / scenario: CST 313 needs both prerequisites
values.Preconditions: The target term is Spring 2027; CST 323 is the companion lab; The fixtures do not skip rules the app is supposed to enforce
values.Inputs / data: CST 313 and CST 323; Only CST 312 completed; Only CST 140 completed; Both completed; Neither completed
values.Procedure:
1. Create each transcript on its own.
2. Submit the add with the companion.
3. Write down what the action did and what the database shows.
values.Expected result: Both CST 312 and CST 140 are required; When both are complete, the pair can be added
values.Pass criterion: Only the try with both completed succeeds; The other three are rejected and do not leave a partial row; A successful pair is 4 credits
values.Evidence to retain: The screen; The action response, with secrets removed; The database before and after

values.Test / scenario: Courses can only be added in terms when they are offered
values.Preconditions: The clock is 2026-02-15; The Spring 2026 plan is acknowledged; Summer, Summer I, Summer II, and Fall 2026 are available; CST 112 is completed, which CST 212 needs; The student is a senior, which CST 496 needs
values.Inputs / data: CST 212 and CST 222 in Spring, then in Summer, Summer I, Summer II, and Fall; CST 225 and CST 235 in Fall, then in Spring; CST 496 in Spring, then in Fall, with the approved senior standing
values.Procedure:
1. Reset for each course and season.
2. Try the add from the screen and from the action.
3. Compare the F, S, and SS values in the source with the term that was stored.
values.Expected result: The CST 212 pair is rejected in Spring and allowed in Fall and in summer, including Summer I and Summer II; The CST 225 pair is rejected in Fall and allowed in Spring; CST 496 is Fall only, and the standing also has to be approved
values.Pass criterion: Every season matches the source; A rejected add names the term or the offering that is not supported; A rejected try leaves no row
values.Evidence to retain: The screen; The action response, with secrets removed; The database before and after

values.Test / scenario: A missing prerequisite stays visible
values.Preconditions: The merged fixture D-02; Do not invent CST 201 or CST 356; The clock allows the term you are testing
values.Inputs / data: CST 240 requires CST 201, and CST 201 is not in the catalog; CST 484 requires CST 356, and CST 356 is not in the catalog; The other missing references listed in the course catalog
values.Procedure:
1. Compare the raw prerequisite text with the merged course codes.
2. Look at the seeded prerequisite groups and options.
3. Try to add CST 240 and CST 484 without the missing course.
4. Confirm the rule did not quietly disappear.
values.Expected result: An unknown prerequisite stays visible and unresolved; The course is blocked, or an academic exception is written down; The current seed drops a group that has no options and no note
values.Pass criterion: Neither course is treated as freely eligible just because its prerequisite is missing; Every catalog row with a missing reference is reviewed
values.Evidence to retain: The screen; The action response, with secrets removed; The database before and after

values.Test / scenario: Standing and consent notes are checked, not ignored
values.Preconditions: Fixture D-04 uses the spring clock, and the target is a fall term; The student's standing is saved on the profile; No consent workflow was found
values.Inputs / data: CST 231 as a freshman, then as a sophomore; CST 317 as a sophomore, then as a junior or senior; CST 460 as a junior, then as a senior; CST 340 with only an instructor-consent note
values.Procedure:
1. Set each standing on its own.
2. Try the course in a term when it is offered and the plan is open.
3. Compare eligibility with the note in the source.
4. For CST 340, try it without CST 140, and with a documented consent only if the app supports that.
values.Expected result: Standing and consent from the catalog are enforced; A sentence in a note is not the same as an approval; The current helper ignores a group that has no options and only a note
values.Pass criterion: Every standing case matches the academic policy that was approved; If consent cannot be recorded, the rule stays unresolved; The note is not treated as a way around the rule
values.Evidence to retain: The screen; The action response, with secrets removed; The database before and after

values.Test / scenario: Keep the broken CST 300 prerequisite text, and do not guess a rule
values.Preconditions: The raw CST file and the seed snapshot are both available; Do not insert a prerequisite you made up
values.Inputs / data: The CST 300 catalog note; The prerequisite sentence that does not parse
values.Procedure:
1. Open the CST 300 details.
2. Compare the description and the prerequisite note with the raw source.
3. Review it with the advisor who owns the academic decision.
4. Check that eligibility follows the rule they confirm, and not a guess.
values.Expected result: The broken text stays visible as an unresolved source problem; No course dependency is invented; The course is not treated as eligible just because the text is unclear
values.Pass criterion: The source text is not lost; The academic owner writes down the real rule before eligibility is accepted
values.Evidence to retain: The source text next to what the app shows; The academic owner's note

values.Test / scenario: Technical electives follow the real Information Technology and Electronics Technology pools
values.Preconditions: One Information Technology 2025 profile and one Electronics Technology 2025 profile; Fixture D-02
values.Inputs / data: CST 101; CST 306; CST 120; CST 212; A search for the technical group
values.Procedure:
1. Search Technical Electives in each student's course browser.
2. Write down the whole pool.
3. Compare what is excluded, and the number limits, with the seed and with catalog.ts.
values.Expected result: Information Technology currently uses any CST course, with no minimum number; Electronics Technology uses CST 200 or above; Courses that are already required are left out of the pool; CST 306 is a candidate in both pools; CST 120 is in neither technical pool; CST 212 is core for Electronics Technology and a candidate for Information Technology
values.Pass criterion: The pools match the program baseline that was approved; CST 101 showing up only for Information Technology is a question for Q-03; Do not assume every program uses a 200-level rule
values.Evidence to retain: The pools from each browser; The comparison with the seed

values.Test / scenario: Management and general education courses show up in the right pools
values.Preconditions: The merged seed from fixture D-02; Look at Information Technology and Electronics Technology separately; General education tags are available
values.Inputs / data: MGMT 110, which is required; MGMT 201, which is an elective; BIOL 100, Scientific Reasoning with lab; ENGL 211, Survey of African-American Literature I, tagged AA; ECEN 121, MEEN 121, and SSFM 226, which were skipped

2. Check whether MGMT 110 is required or elective in each program.
3. Write down that BIOL 100 includes a lab.
4. Confirm the skipped rows are not courses someone can select.

values.Pass criterion: The full pools match the source and the program rules that were approved; A required course is not also counted as an elective; Unmatched rows are excluded
values.Evidence to retain: The pools; The tags; The skipped rows

values.Test / scenario: An unlisted course can be saved only as a free elective
values.Preconditions: The student has an Information Technology free-elective slot; SSFM 226 is in the source list but was not seeded, because its general education row did not match; The title comes from the source; Use 3 credits in this fixture until the real credits are confirmed
values.Inputs / data: Free elective: SSFM 226, A Personal Approach to Health, 3 fixture credits, marked Transfer; The same course placed in a technical slot; A course number of 099; A missing title; 0 credits, and 7 credits
values.Procedure:
1. Enter the external course in the free-elective slot.
2. Save and reload.
3. Try the same course in a restricted slot, and try the bad number, title, and credit values.
values.Expected result: An unlisted course numbered 100 or higher, with 1 to 6 credits, saves only as a free elective; A transfer is stored as completed, with source TRANSFER and grade TR; The catalog course id is empty, and the code and title are kept
values.Pass criterion: The valid free-elective entry is still there after a reload; The five bad or restricted tries are rejected and leave no partial data; The code and title are real; The 3-credit value is a test assumption until a transcript or catalog confirms it
values.Evidence to retain: The saved free-elective row; The rejected tries

values.Test / scenario: The same course cannot complete two slots
values.Preconditions: Information Technology, with CST 120 already completed; Technical and free slots are available; CST 306 is a real catalog option; The counting rules in Q-05 are approved
values.Inputs / data: CST 306 marked complete in two slots; CST 120 as its named completion and again as a free elective; The same course id sent twice in one save
values.Procedure:
1. Submit each duplicate through save transcript progress, one at a time.
2. Check the duplicate error and that the save rolled back.
3. As a control, save one valid CST 306 claim.
values.Expected result: Each course is recorded once across named courses and slots; A course that already fills a named requirement cannot also fill the free slot
values.Pass criterion: Duplicate claims are rejected; A rejected save does not leave part of the transcript behind; The control saves one 3-credit entry
values.Evidence to retain: The error; The transcript before and after

values.Test / scenario: Submit a plan, approve it with a PIN, and confirm registration
values.Preconditions: Student A is assigned to advisor A-1; The Spring 2027 draft includes CST 130; CST 130 is not already on the transcript
values.Inputs / data: The student submits the term; Advisor A-1 uses PIN TEST1234; The student marks the term registered
values.Procedure:
1. The student submits the plan.
2. Confirm it is waiting for advisor A-1.
3. Approve it with the PIN.
4. Check the student's view of the PIN and the transcript.
5. The student confirms they registered, then tries that action again.
values.Expected result: The plan moves from draft to submitted to approved; Approval immediately records CST 130 as in progress, source NCAT, at 3 credits; Confirmation sets the registered time; This is not official enrollment, and it does not add a second transcript row
values.Pass criterion: The status and the times are right; The PIN matches exactly; There is one in-progress row before and after confirmation; Confirming a second time is refused; The completion percent does not count an in-progress course as finished
values.Evidence to retain: The screen at each step; The action response, with the PIN handled carefully; The database before and after

values.Test / scenario: Only the assigned advisor can approve, and only with a valid PIN
values.Preconditions: A submitted plan for student A, assigned to advisor A-1; A fresh fixture for each try
values.Inputs / data: PIN ABC, which is 3 characters; PIN ABCD, which is 4; A PIN of 12 letters or numbers; A PIN of 13 letters or numbers; PIN AB-CD; Advisor A-2, who is not assigned; A student trying to approve; The same action on a draft, and on a plan that is already approved
values.Procedure:
1. Try each PIN length and format.
2. Try an advisor who is not assigned, and try the student role.
3. Try a draft and a plan that is already approved.
4. Check the status and the transcript.
values.Expected result: Only the assigned advisor can approve a submitted plan; The PIN, after trimming, must be 4 to 12 letters or numbers
values.Pass criterion: 4 characters and 12 characters are valid; Other PINs, roles, and plan states are rejected; A rejected try does not create an in-progress transcript row

values.Test / scenario: Only a draft can be edited, and an empty plan cannot be submitted
values.Preconditions: Use student A's real plan and course ids; One draft contains CST 130; A separate draft is empty
values.Inputs / data: Submit the empty draft; Add and remove on a draft; Add and remove after it is submitted; Add and remove after it is approved
values.Procedure:
1. Submit the empty draft.
2. Edit the draft that has CST 130, and confirm that works.
3. Submit it, then try to add and to remove.
4. Approve it, and try both changes again.
values.Expected result: An empty plan is rejected; Only a draft can be edited; The approved course list stays protected
values.Pass criterion: The empty submission fails; The allowed draft edits stick; All four locked changes are rejected and do not change a row
values.Evidence to retain: The plan status at each step; The rows before and after

values.Test / scenario: The planner only offers terms that exist for this date
values.Preconditions: The academic terms from the seed; The date is fixed at 2026-10-11; There is no current plan, and notTakingTermId is empty
values.Inputs / data: The prompt before any choice; Choosing to plan Fall 2026; Declining Fall 2026; Spring 2027; Fall 2027, which is not in the seed
values.Procedure:
1. Open the planner before answering the prompt.
2. Choose to take the current semester and write down which terms appear.
3. Reset, decline the current semester, and write down the terms.
4. Repeat with the clock at 2026-02-15.
values.Expected result: Before the choice, there are no planning terms; Accepting the current semester adds a Fall 2026 draft and Spring 2027; Declining leaves only Spring 2027; With the clock in February 2026, the terms are the current spring plus Summer, Summer I, Summer II, and Fall 2026
values.Pass criterion: The terms on the screen match the seed for that date and that choice; The test never tries to use a Fall 2027 term that does not exist
values.Evidence to retain: The terms shown for each choice; The date used

values.Test / scenario: An earlier planned course can satisfy the next term
values.Preconditions: The date is fixed at 2026-10-11; Fall 2026 is the current draft; Spring 2027 is the target; MATH 110 and CST 120 are not on the transcript
values.Inputs / data: CST 120 on Fall 2026, then CST 112 and CST 122 on Spring 2027; A second try with CST 120 only on the same Spring plan
values.Procedure:
1. Add CST 120 to Fall 2026.
2. Add the pair to Spring 2027.
3. Reset, and put CST 120 only on the Spring plan.
4. Try the pair again.
values.Expected result: The code counts a prerequisite planned in an earlier term; It does not count a prerequisite planned in the same term; The academic owner still has to approve whether a planned course should count before it is taken
values.Pass criterion: The earlier-plan try adds the pair; The same-term try is rejected; A rejected try does not leave half of the pair
values.Evidence to retain: Both plans; The action result

values.Test / scenario: A transcript dated in the future does not count as a past prerequisite
values.Preconditions: An isolated transcript fixture; The target is the same Spring 2027; MATH 110 is not available as the other option
values.Inputs / data: CST 120 in progress, or completed, on a Summer 2027 transcript; The same course on a Fall 2026 transcript, as the comparison
values.Procedure:
1. Load the future-dated transcript in the isolated fixture.
2. Try to add CST 112 and CST 122 for Spring 2027.
3. Reset and use the earlier-term transcript as the control.
values.Expected result: If prerequisites have to come first in time, Summer 2027 coursework cannot satisfy Spring 2027; The current transcript query ignores the term date
values.Pass criterion: The future-dated try is rejected, or an approved exception is written down; The earlier completion is accepted
values.Evidence to retain: The transcript dates; The result of each try

values.Test / scenario: A minimum grade is separate from the course status
values.Preconditions: Information Technology core requires at least a C; There is no grade screen; The isolated fixtures set the grade and the transcript status directly
values.Inputs / data: CST 120 completed with a C; CST 120 completed with a C-minus; CST 120 completed with an F; Then try CST 112 and CST 122; A control where CST 120 has status Failed
values.Procedure:
1. Set up each grade and status on its own.
2. Check the credit total and whether the later course is eligible.
3. Compare that with the signed grade rule and the signed prerequisite rule.
values.Expected result: A C meets the Information Technology core minimum; A lower grade does not count toward the core; A minimum grade for a prerequisite needs its own approved rule; The helper currently checks the course id and the status, not the grade
values.Pass criterion: Degree credit respects the C minimum; Prerequisite results match the signed academic rule; A failed status is excluded
values.Evidence to retain: The grade and status of each fixture; The credit total and the eligibility result

values.Test / scenario: The course browser and the planner search are not the same list
values.Preconditions: An Information Technology student is missing prerequisites; Spring 2027 is available; No courses are placed in a future term
values.Inputs / data: CST 112, missing its prerequisites; CST 212, which is not offered in Spring; The same exact codes on /student/courses and on /student/planner; A search as the assigned advisor
values.Procedure:
1. Search on each screen.
2. Write down the cards or suggestions, and whether Add is available.
3. Compare that with FR-10, which asks for eligible courses only.
4. Try the search as the assigned advisor, in that student's context.
values.Expected result: The browser currently searches the whole curriculum and can show a course the student cannot take; Planner suggestions use the term and the student's eligibility; Accepting FR-10 means both roles get an agreed list of eligible courses only
values.Pass criterion: The search you are accepting does not include an ineligible course; The advisor can search in the same student's context; The difference is gap G-06; Hiding the Add button is not enough to call the broad list accepted
values.Evidence to retain: Both result lists; Whether Add was available

values.Test / scenario: A lecture and its lab are saved together, or not at all
values.Preconditions: Student A's Spring 2027 draft; MATH 110 is completed; CST 112 and CST 122 are not on the plan; You can force the second insert to fail, in an isolated run
values.Inputs / data: CST 112 plus CST 122; The companion id repeated; CST 130 sent as the companion, which is unrelated; More than 8 companion ids; A valid pair whose second insert fails
values.Procedure:
1. Add a valid pair as the control.
2. Reset and repeat the companion id.
3. Reset and try an unrelated companion, then a list that is too long.
4. Force the second insert of a valid pair to fail.
5. Compare the plan rows.
values.Expected result: A valid list, or a list with the companion repeated, saves one lecture and one lab; An unrelated companion or a list that is too long is rejected; If the transaction fails, both courses roll back
values.Pass criterion: There is no duplicate and no half pair; A rejected try saves zero rows of the pair; The error is shown, and rows that were already there stay as they were
values.Evidence to retain: The rows after each try; The error when the insert fails

values.Test / scenario: The merged seed matches the sources, including courses that are missing
values.Preconditions: A read-only snapshot of the sources; An isolated database that was seeded on purpose; Never run the seed against production
values.Inputs / data: 65 CST rows; 32 management rows; 106 general education rows, including 3 that are skipped; 199 distinct courses the seed can load; 202 rows in the catalog review
values.Procedure:
1. Compare each course code, title, credits, and offering with the merged sources.
2. Confirm the general education filters that match, and the handbook fallback.
3. Check prerequisite groups for AND and OR, and check that lecture and lab pairs point at each other.
4. Check the missing references listed in the catalog.
values.Expected result: On a clean database, exactly 199 distinct source courses are represented; The three unmatched general education rows are skipped; Where a CST title or credit differs from the handbook, the CST value wins; The raw prerequisite text is reviewed against the groups that were stored
values.Pass criterion: The source snapshot matches the clean isolated database; A required course is not quietly dropped; Every missing predecessor and every note-only rule is dealt with before academic validation is approved
values.Evidence to retain: The counts; The list of missing references; The comparison notes

values.Baseline requirement (faithful summary): A student signs in with an email and password, and can reset a forgotten password.
A student can see the requirements for their own program.
A student can add a course when it follows the rules.
A student can remove a course from the degree plan.
Each term checks prerequisites and courses that must be taken together before the plan is accepted.
An advisor can change a plan by hand and leave comments.
The app shows how much of the degree is finished, as a percentage. The source document calls this “grade degree.”
A person has to sign in before they can see a plan. The source still says username and password.
When something goes wrong, the person sees an error.
Students and advisors can search for courses that fit that student's situation. The source says the list should include only eligible courses.
The app works in current web browsers.
A page loads within 5 seconds on a 100 to 200 Mbps connection, with up to 500 people using the app at once.
The app signs a person out after 30 minutes with nothing happening.
A person can finish a common task in fewer than 5 clicks.
Data is backed up every day, and a backup can be restored.
Adding or removing a course is saved within 15 seconds, or the person sees an error.
People only see and change what their role allows.
After a failure, the app is usable again within 3 minutes, and academic data that was already saved is still there.
At least 500 people can use the app at once without it slowing down.
Plans and schedules are encrypted, and student data is protected in the way the FERPA note describes.
A person using a keyboard or a screen reader can complete the same tasks. The source points to WCAG.

The acceptance baseline is Functional Requirements.pdf and the Final Requirement Specs, pages 7 to 15. Source notes R-01 through R-10 and the course catalog record the project snapshot. Notes from reading the code are not test results.

values.Proposed control / decision: Keep the FR-06 tests for manual changes and comments as missing-workflow gaps. Add tests for the assigned advisor's PIN, for locking a plan, and for two saves at once.

values.Source gap or constraint: The tasks and their starting screens are not specified; Keyboard use is not called equivalent; The final spec has no satisfaction target

values.Proposed control / decision: An academic reviewer settles the policy and the text. Add tests for standing, consent, and the broken CST 300 text before calling FR-05 covered.

values.Issue / risk: Degree progress on the dashboard is stuck at zero

values.Proposed control / decision: Recheck the rules when the plan is submitted and when it is reviewed. Test a stale write from a second tab. Do not approve an invalid plan quietly.

values.Issue / risk: The save deadline and the failure path are untested

values.Proposed control / decision: Run the timeout and failure tests. Confirm the pair rolls back together, and that the person sees an error and a screen that matches what was saved.

values.Issue / risk: Backups and encryption have to be proved outside the app

values.Proposed control / decision: List the stores that actually hold the data. Collect sanitized proof of backup, restore, and encryption from the provider. Do not invent a Redis or S3 setup.
